metadata.description: Educational medical glossary for common lab test terms
metadata.disclaimer: This glossary is for educational purposes only and does not constitute medical advice.

hemoglobin.definition: A protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen from the lungs to the rest of the body and returns carbon dioxide back to the lungs.
hemoglobin.clinical_significance: Low levels indicate anaemia; high levels may suggest polycythaemia or dehydration.

rbc.definition: The number of red blood cells per volume of blood. Red blood cells carry oxygen throughout the body.
rbc.clinical_significance: Low RBC may indicate anaemia or blood loss; high RBC may indicate polycythaemia.

wbc.definition: The number of white blood cells per volume of blood. White blood cells are part of the immune system and help the body fight infection.
wbc.clinical_significance: High WBC (leukocytosis) may indicate infection or inflammation; low WBC (leukopenia) may indicate bone marrow problems or autoimmune disease.

platelets.definition: Platelets are tiny blood cells that help the body form clots to stop bleeding.
platelets.clinical_significance: Low platelets (thrombocytopenia) increase bleeding risk; high platelets (thrombocytosis) may increase clotting risk.

glucose.definition: The amount of glucose (sugar) in the blood. Glucose is the main source of energy for the body's cells.
glucose.clinical_significance: High fasting glucose may indicate diabetes or pre-diabetes; low glucose (hypoglycaemia) can cause dizziness and confusion.

cholesterol.definition: A waxy, fat-like substance found in all cells of the body. Measured as total cholesterol, which includes LDL, HDL, and VLDL.
cholesterol.clinical_significance: High cholesterol increases the risk of heart disease and stroke.

creatinine.definition: A waste product produced by normal muscle metabolism, filtered out of the blood by the kidneys. Used to assess kidney function.
creatinine.clinical_significance: High creatinine may indicate impaired kidney function or kidney disease.

vitamin_d.definition: A fat-soluble vitamin essential for calcium absorption, bone health, and immune function. Measured as 25-hydroxyvitamin D in the blood.
vitamin_d.clinical_significance: Deficiency is linked to bone disorders, weakened immunity, and muscle weakness.

tsh.definition: A hormone produced by the pituitary gland that stimulates the thyroid gland to produce thyroid hormones (T3 and T4).
tsh.clinical_significance: High TSH suggests an underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism); low TSH suggests an overactive thyroid (hyperthyroidism).

hematocrit.definition: The proportion of red blood cells in the total volume of blood, expressed as a percentage.
hematocrit.clinical_significance: Low hematocrit indicates anaemia; high hematocrit may suggest dehydration or polycythaemia.
